name: Syngenta Icon 10CS Mosquito Insecticide
lead: Mbu (mosquitoes) bite at dusk and through the night, and they can carry diseases such as malaria. Syngenta Icon 10CS is a long-lasting residual insecticide: you dilute it with water, spray it on the surfaces where insects rest, and it keeps working after the spray has dried. It contains lambda-cyhalothrin 100 g/L in a capsule suspension (CS) formulation and is also used against flies and cockroaches. The 62.5 ml bottle suits a house, a few rooms or a small business.
features: Lambda-cyhalothrin 100 g/L public health insecticide
Capsule suspension (CS) with long-lasting residual action
Controls mosquitoes, flies and cockroaches
Diluted with water and sprayed on resting surfaces
62.5 ml pack for a house or small business
Delivered to all 47 counties
specs: Target pests: Mosquitoes, flies and cockroaches
Dilution: as directed on the label
helps: In a capsule suspension the active ingredient is held in tiny capsules in a liquid. After spraying, the capsules stay on the treated surface and release the active ingredient slowly, which is designed to give a longer-lasting residual effect than a spray that is released all at once.
use: Shake the bottle well, measure carefully as the label directs and mix thoroughly in clean water in the sprayer. Spray the surfaces where insects rest or walk: walls, door and window frames, eaves, shaded places, drains, and the cracks and corners where cockroaches hide. Treat the whole house in one session so insects do not move to an untreated room. For large buildings, consider a licensed pest control operator.
before: Remove or cover food, dishes and water containers
Keep people and pets out of the treated rooms until the spray has dried
Clear stagnant water, rubbish and blocked drains to cut breeding sites
Fit mosquito nets and window screens for added protection
safety: Read the label before use. Wear gloves, a mask, goggles and protective clothing when mixing and spraying, and wash well afterwards. Keep away from children, pets, food and water. Lambda-cyhalothrin is very toxic to fish and bees, so never rinse sprayers or containers into drains, streams, ponds or fish tanks.
storage: Keep in the original closed bottle in a cool, dry, locked place away from food and feed.
faq: What does capsule suspension (CS) mean?
The active ingredient is held in tiny capsules that stay on the treated surface and release it slowly. This is designed to last longer than a spray that acts all at once.
Which insects is Icon 10CS used against?
It is sold for public health insects, including mosquitoes, flies and cockroaches, in homes and small businesses.
Is the 62.5 ml pack enough for my house?
It is a convenient size for a house, a few rooms or a small business. A large building may need more than one pack, or a licensed pest control operator.

name: Bayer Baraki Pellets Rat and Mice Poison
lead: Rats gnaw wiring, foul food stores and spread disease, and a few quickly become many. Bayer Baraki Pellets are a ready-to-use rodenticide bait made for single-feed control: rats and mice need to eat the bait only once. The pellets contain difethialone, an anticoagulant, and need no mixing. Baraki comes as a 10 g sachet, a 100 g pack and a 1 kg box.
features: Single-feed anticoagulant bait for roof rats, Norway rats and house mice
Mould and moisture resistant, so it stays attractive in damp stores
Sold as effective against resistant strains
Suited to homes, markets, farms and industrial sites
specs: Product: Baraki Pellets Rat and Mice Poison
Pack sizes: 10 g sachet, 100 g, 1 kg box
helps: Rodents chew wiring, sacks and packaging, eat and spoil stored food, and leave droppings and urine that spread germs. Roof rats climb into ceilings and stores, Norway rats burrow along walls and drains, and house mice nest in small hidden spaces, so the places to bait differ. Pellets that resist mould and moisture help in damp stores and farm buildings, where loose bait goes off quickly.
dose: Rats: 50 to 75 g per station (about 5 to 7 sachets of 10 g), one station every 5 to 10 m along walls, rat runs, burrows and sheltered areas
Mice: 15 to 20 g per station (about 2 sachets of 10 g), one station every 2 to 4 m along walls, runways and nests
A 100 g pack is about 10 sachets of 10 g, and a 1 kg box is about 100 sachets
use: Inspect first for droppings, gnaw marks, runs and burrows, so you know where the rodents travel. Place the bait in covered bait stations or tamper-resistant boxes, never loose on the floor. Check every 2 to 3 days and top up until feeding stops. Wearing gloves, collect dead rodents and dispose of them safely.
before: Block holes and gaps around pipes, doors and roof edges
Store grain, feed and food in closed containers, off the floor
Remove rubbish and clutter that give rodents shelter
safety: This is a poison. Read the label before use and keep the bait out of reach of children, pets and poultry. Wear gloves and wash your hands after handling it. If a person or an animal swallows any, get medical or veterinary help immediately and show the pack.
storage: Keep sachets and packs closed in a dry, locked place, away from food, animal feed and children.
faq: Which Baraki pack size should I buy?
The 10 g sachet suits one room or a first trial. The 100 g pack suits a shop, a store or a home with several bait points, and the 1 kg box suits farms, markets and industrial sites.
Does Baraki need mixing?
No. The pellets are ready to use, so you simply place them in covered bait stations.
How often should I check the stations?
Every 2 to 3 days, topping up until feeding stops. Read the label on your pack as well.

name: Bromarat 0.005 RB Rodent Bait
lead: Bromarat 0.005 RB is a ready-to-use rodent bait for rats and mice, made to be used inside bait stations. There is nothing to mix: you fill the stations and place them where the rodents travel. It comes in a 25 g pack for homes and small stores and a 100 g pack for stores, farms and larger premises.
features: Ready-to-use rodent bait for rats and mice
Designed for use inside bait stations
Two pack sizes: 25 g and 100 g
25 g for homes and small stores, 100 g for farms and larger premises
Delivered to all 47 counties
specs: Directions: as printed on the manufacturer's label
helps: A bait station is a small covered box or tube that holds the bait. It keeps the bait dry and clean, makes it harder for children, pets and livestock to reach it, and gives rodents a dark, sheltered place where they feel safe to feed. Stations also show you how much has been eaten, so you learn where the rodents are most active.
use: Place stations along walls, near holes and burrows, behind cupboards and stacked goods, and on runs where you see droppings and gnaw marks. A home or small shop usually needs a few; a store or farm needs more, spaced as the label advises. Check them regularly, top up bait that has been eaten and replace bait that is wet or mouldy. Carry on until no more bait is taken, then remove the stations and leftover bait as the label directs.
before: Walk around the building and look for droppings, gnaw marks and runs
Store food and grain in closed containers and stack bags away from the walls
Block holes around pipes and doors
Clear rubbish and long grass near the building
safety: Check the PCPB registration number on the label and read the label before use. Keep children, pets and livestock away from the bait and the stations, and never put bait where food, feed or drinking water could be contaminated. Wear gloves, wash your hands afterwards and dispose of dead rodents safely. If anyone swallows the bait, get medical help at once and show the label; if an animal eats it, call a vet.
storage: Keep the pack tightly closed, in a cool, dry, locked place out of reach of children and pets.
faq: Why use a bait station instead of leaving bait on the floor?
A station keeps the bait dry and clean, makes it harder for children, pets and livestock to reach it, and gives rodents a sheltered place to feed.
Which Bromarat pack suits my building?
The 25 g pack suits a home or a small shop with a few stations. The 100 g pack suits stores, farms and larger premises with many.
How long should I keep baiting?
Keep checking and topping up until no more bait is taken, then remove the stations and leftover bait as the label directs.

name: Fuko-Kil Rat Poison
lead: Fuko-Kil is a rodenticide for rats and moles in homes, stores and farms in Kenya. Rats spoil food and gnaw wires, while moles (fuko) tunnel through lawns, gardens and fields and damage the roots of young plants, and Fuko-Kil is sold for both. The small 25 g pack suits a home or a small farm that needs to treat a limited area.
features: Rodenticide for rats and moles
Small 25 g pack for homes and small farms
For use in homes, stores and farms
Delivered to all 47 counties
specs: Directions: follow the label for placement and quantity
helps: Rats eat and spoil stored food, gnaw wires, packaging and furniture, and spread germs through droppings and urine. They breed fast, so a small problem soon becomes a large one. Moles push up mounds of soil and cut tunnels through lawns, gardens and fields, which matters on small farms and in kitchen gardens where young plants have shallow roots.
use: Follow the label for placement and quantity. For rats, put small amounts of bait in protected spots near nesting holes, along walls and on runs where you see droppings and gnaw marks, using a covered tray or bait station where possible. For moles, follow the label's directions for placing the product in active runs, and do not spread it on the soil surface where other animals could find it. Replace bait that has been eaten or has got wet, and stop when the activity ends.
before: Keep food, grain and feed in closed containers
Seal holes, gaps and cracks, and clear rubbish and long grass near buildings
Look for fresh mounds and runs so you know where the moles are active
Choose spots that children, pets and poultry cannot reach
safety: Check the PCPB registration number on the label and read it before use. Keep Fuko-Kil away from children, pets, poultry and other animals, and never place it where food, feed or water can be contaminated. Collect dead rodents regularly, wearing gloves, and wash your hands after handling bait. If anyone swallows it, get medical help at once and show the pack; if an animal eats it, contact a vet immediately.
storage: Close the pack tightly after each use and keep it locked away, cool and dry, away from food.
faq: Can Fuko-Kil be used for both rats and moles?
It is sold for rats and moles. Placement differs for each, so follow the label for rats in buildings and for moles in active runs.
Is the 25 g pack enough?
It is a small pack for a home or a small farm treating a limited area. A large store or farm will need more bait than one pack.
What should I do with leftover bait?
Remove leftover bait at the end of the treatment and follow the label for disposal. Wash your hands afterwards.

name: Miratex Pellets Rat and Mice Killer Bait
lead: Miratex pellets are a ready-to-use bait for rat and mice control in homes, shops, kitchens, stores and farm buildings. There is no mixing: you place the pellets near nesting holes, along walls and on rat runs. The 20 g pack suits a single room, a small store or a first treatment, and the 240 g pack is made for warehouses, hotels, farms and other larger premises that need many bait points.
features: Pellet bait for rat and mice control
Ready to use, with no mixing
Placed near nesting holes, along walls and on rat runs
Two pack sizes: 20 g and 240 g
Delivered to all 47 counties
specs: Product: Rat and mice killer bait pellets
helps: Rodents usually move along walls and through dark, quiet corners. They contaminate food, chew wires, damage sacks and furniture, and can spread disease, and because they breed fast, early baiting together with good hygiene is the sensible way to protect a home, a business and stored produce. Larger buildings need bait in many places and need it topped up over time, which is what the 240 g pack is for: grain stores, feed stores, poultry houses, workshops and godowns.
use: Walk around first and look for droppings, gnaw marks, greasy rub marks along walls and burrows. Put bait close to those signs, along walls and near nesting holes, at points that children, pets and livestock cannot reach. Check the bait points often and replace pellets that have been eaten. Wearing gloves, remove dead rodents safely.
before: Keep grain and animal feed in sealed containers, on raised pallets in stores
Block holes and gaps, and cut tall grass close to buildings
Keep rubbish and old materials away from the walls
Count the bait points you need before you choose a pack size
safety: Check the PCPB registration number on the label and read the label before use. Place the bait where only rodents can reach it, and never near food for people or animals, or inside food containers. Keep it away from children, pets and livestock, and wash your hands after handling it.
storage: Store the pellets in their closed pack, somewhere dry and secure, away from food and out of reach of children.
faq: Which Miratex pack should I buy?
The 20 g pack suits a single room, a small store or a first treatment. The 240 g pack suits stores, farms, warehouses and hotels that need many bait points.
Do I need to mix the pellets?
No. They are ready to use, so you place them directly at the bait points.
Where do rats usually travel?
Along walls, through dark corners and between their nest and their food. Bait close to droppings, gnaw marks and runways works better than bait in the middle of a room.

It is for warehouses, stores and farm buildings where many bait points are needed, such as grain stores, feed stores, godowns, hotels and poultry houses.
Where should the bait stations go?
Along walls, behind stacked goods, near holes and on rat runs, in covered stations that only rodents can reach.
Is baiting enough on its own?
Baiting is strongest when it is paired with good sanitation and proofing: raised pallets, sealed gaps, covered drains and cleared rubbish and bush.

name: Rodilon Wax Blocks
lead: Rodilon wax blocks are a rodent bait for rats and mice in damp areas, stores and farms. Loose baits can soften, grow mould or lose their appeal when they get wet, while a wax block is made to hold up in damp and humid places. The 10 g pack is a small size for kitchens, drains, small stores and sheds, so you can bait one trouble spot without buying a large pack.
features: Wax block bait for rats and mice
Holds up in damp and humid places
Useful where loose pellets could be carried off or scattered
Small 10 g pack for homes, kitchens and sheds
Delivered to all 47 counties
helps: Wax blocks are made to resist moisture, so they stay in good condition for longer in basements, drains, cellars, stores near the kitchen, farm sheds and poultry houses. Rats and mice can gnaw the blocks, and because a block is solid it is also useful where pellets might be carried off or scattered.
use: Put blocks along walls, near holes and burrows, behind appliances and in dark corners where you see droppings or gnaw marks. In a damp area, keep them above the wet floor where you can, inside covered bait stations that keep out children, pets and livestock. Check them often and replace any block that has been eaten or damaged.
before: Fix leaking pipes that give rodents water
Store grain and feed in sealed containers
Block gaps around pipes, doors and roofs
Keep rubbish covered and take it out regularly
safety: Check the PCPB registration number on the label and read the label before use. Keep the blocks away from children, pets and livestock, wear gloves to handle them, and wash your hands afterwards. Collect dead rodents with gloves and dispose of them safely.
storage: Keep unused blocks in their pack, dry and out of reach, away from food and animal feed.
faq: Why choose a wax block instead of pellets?
Blocks are made to resist moisture, so they hold up in damp places where loose pellets can go mouldy or spoil quickly.
Where should I place Rodilon blocks?
Along walls, near holes and burrows, behind appliances and in dark corners, above any wet floor, in covered stations that keep children and pets away.
What else helps in a damp store?
Fix leaking pipes, seal gaps around pipes, doors and roofs, store grain in sealed containers and keep rubbish covered.

name: Gradometer 480EC Termiticide
lead: Mchwa (termites) feed on wood, paper and other plant material, and they can weaken roof timbers, door frames, fence posts and furniture before the damage is clearly visible. Gradometer 480EC is an emulsifiable concentrate termiticide containing chlorpyrifos 480 g/L, supplied in a 1 litre bottle. It is used for treating timber, trees and fencing poles, wooden structures, and termite nests in lawns and gardens.
features: Emulsifiable concentrate (EC) termiticide
Active ingredient: chlorpyrifos 480 g/L
For timber in buildings and construction, trees and fencing poles
For treating termite nests in lawns and gardens
1 litre bottle
Delivered to all 47 counties
specs: Dilution: as printed on the manufacturer's label
helps: In gardens and lawns termites build nests and mounds, and they can attack the roots of young plants and trees. Indoors and around the home they eat into timber in buildings and construction, trees and fencing poles, and wooden structures such as sheds, posts and frames. Early treatment limits the damage and the cost of repairs.
use: Gradometer 480EC is an emulsifiable concentrate, so it is diluted with water as directed on the label. Use the label dilution for timber and for nests, and never mix it stronger than recommended. Treat timber thoroughly, paying attention to cut ends, joints and the places where wood touches the soil. For a nest, follow the label instructions for reaching it and treating the soil around it.
before: Remove old stumps, dead wood and rotting timber from around buildings
Keep timber off the ground where possible, and keep it dry
Fix leaking pipes and drains that keep the soil damp
Inspect timber regularly for mud tubes, soft wood and flying termites
safety: Check the PCPB registration number on the label and mix and apply exactly as directed. Wear protective gear, including gloves, a mask, goggles and protective clothing, and keep away from children, pets, food and water. Chlorpyrifos is harmful to fish and aquatic life, so keep it away from streams, ponds, wells and drains. For buildings, consider a licensed pest control operator.
storage: Store in the original closed bottle in a cool, dry, locked place away from food and feed.
faq: What can I treat with Gradometer 480EC?
It is used for timber in buildings and construction, trees and fencing poles, wooden structures such as sheds, posts and frames, and termite nests in lawns and gardens.
Can I use it on a termite mound in my garden?
It is used for treating termite nests in lawns and gardens. Follow the label instructions for reaching the nest and treating the soil around it.
Does treatment replace good housekeeping?
No. Remove stumps and rotting wood, keep timber dry and off the ground, fix leaks and inspect timber for mud tubes so that termites have fewer reasons to return.
